title: feat(messaging): organization administrators send in-app messages from Setup
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu3fM4vyqPaHhqDwy7WEqQAh)_

Fixes #32445 (PR 2 of 2)

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：Setup → 诊断 → 通知事件列表的工具栏多了「发送站内消息」动作，组织管理员可以发给本组织所有人，或挑选本组织成员，填标题、正文、级别和可选链接；背后是新路由 `POST /api/v1/messaging/in-app-messages`，经 `emit()` 单一入口只走站内通道，成功后回答发给了几个人。
- 为什么改：裁决 6810324463 选 A 的第二期（第一期 #32782 已合并 `org:members`）；对话框是 ui 卡 #32796，本 PR 不碰 `ui/**`。
- 风险与回滚：门是当前组织里的 `setup.write`，动作的 `requiredPermissions` 读同一个能力（席位已同意，沿用裁决 6670707546 等两处先例）；组织只取调用者的当前组织，请求体不收组织；挑选的人必须是本组织成员，否则点名拒绝、一条不发。新增一条公开 REST 路由（Clause-② yes）。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/services/service-messaging/src/in-app-message-routes.ts`（门的判定顺序与 `parseInAppMessageBody`）、`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-notification.object.ts`（动作与表单）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging exec vitest run src/in-app-message-routes.integration.test.ts src/in-app-message-action.test.ts`，应见 37 个全绿：A 组织管理员发「全组织」只到 A 的 4 人，B 组织的人一个没收到；B 组织管理员发「全组织」只到 B 的人，A 的人一个没收到。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Ruling 6810324463 on #32445, letter A (the maintainer, verbatim: 「32443 直接做 B，其他同意」), second of its two PRs: the Setup action "Send in-app message", organization administrators only, and the server door it calls. PR 1 (#32782, merged) added the `org:members` audience this door sends "everyone" through. The dialog is the `domain:ui` card #32796; this PR touches nothing under `ui/`.

- **`@objectstack/service-messaging`: the door, `POST /api/v1/messaging/in-app-messages`** (`in-app-message-routes.ts`). In this order, before anything is read:
  1. the caller, resolved by the platform's one request-to-context composition (`resolveRequestExecutionContext`, through `resolveMessagingCaller`), with a permission store or API-key lifecycle refusal relayed as declared;
  2. a held sign-in (ADR-0069), refused with the policy's own code;
  3. anonymous, `401`;
  4. any query parameter, `400` naming it (the closed set is empty);
  5. the capability: `setup.write` in the caller's current organization (`ExecutionContext.systemPermissions`), else `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` naming it;
  6. the organization: the caller's current one (`ExecutionContext.tenantId`); a request with none is refused `403`. There is no organization in the body, and a body that carries `organizationId` or `organization_id` is refused, saying so.

  The body is a closed set, `{ everyone, recipients, title, body, severity, link }`: either `everyone: true` or a `recipients` list of user ids (trimmed, de-duplicated, at most 1,000), not both and not neither; `title` required, at most 255 characters (the inbox title column's width); `body` required, at most 10,000; `severity` `info` (the default), `warning` or `critical`, the event's own options; `link` optional, a path on this site (one leading `/`) or an `http(s)` URL, at most 255. A key outside the set is refused by name, never dropped, and every refusal ends "Nothing was sent."

  Picked recipients are read against `sys_member` of the caller's current organization (`organization_id` and the picked ids, in chunks of 100, projected to `user_id`, under the fan-out's system posture `FAN_OUT_SYSTEM_CONTEXT`). Any id that is not a member is refused `400` by name, and nothing is sent. Every picked id is then addressed as `user:ID`, so no id is ever read as an audience selector or an address.

  The send is one `emit()`: topic `org.announcement`, audience `org:members` (everyone) or the `user:` selectors, `organizationId` the caller's, `actorId` the caller, `payload { title, body, url }`, channels `['inbox']`. The answer is `{ notificationId, recipients, delivered, enqueued, failed }`, with `recipients` the number of distinct people a delivery was made for. No messaging service or data engine: `503` before anything is sent. A membership read or an `emit()` that throws: `500` with the door's sentence, the error in the fault log.
- **The door is mounted by `MessagingServicePlugin`** beside the notification-preference options door, on the same HTTP server (the private mount method is renamed `mountHttpDoors`). The two doors now resolve the caller through one shared module, `messaging-request-caller.ts`, extracted from the preference-options door unchanged; its tests pass as before.
- **The route ledger** (`messaging-route-ledger.ts`) gains the row `POST /api/v1/messaging/in-app-messages`, disposition `server-only`, and its conformance test enumerates the new registrar.
- **`@objectstack/platform-objects`: the action `send_in_app_message` on `sys_notification`**, list toolbar of Setup → Diagnostics → Notification Events, the list every message it sends appears on as one event. A same-origin `type: 'api'` action whose `target` is the door, `requiredPermissions: ['setup.write']`, the door's own capability, so it is listed to exactly the callers the door admits and the action doors refuse anyone else before forwarding (ADR-0066 D4). Its params are the door's body set, one per key: `everyone` (boolean), `recipients` (`user`, multiple), `title` and `body` (required), `severity` (field-backed on the event's own `severity` field, default `info`), `link` (url). A param's visibility cannot read a sibling param, so "either everyone or recipients" is judged at the door, whose refusal names the fix. The confirmation reads "Message sent. Recipients: N" from the door's `recipients`. `ai.exposed` with a description naming the params.
- **Translations.** The action's labels, help texts and confirmation are translated in all ten translated locales (zh-CN, zh-Hant, ja-JP, ko, es-ES, pt-BR, fr, de, ru, ar). Where the word is the English one (`Link` in de and pt-BR), the bundle records the leaf as a copy of the source, as it does for other such leaves.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx` gains "Send a message to your organization": who can send, who receives, the limits, the confirmation, the topic, the REST call, and `org:members` for flows; plus a Quick paths row and a "where is everything" row.

## Tests

- `in-app-message-routes.integration.test.ts` (new), on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3), `single` posture, the platform's `SysMember`, `SysUser` and `SysNotification`, and a real `MessagingService` with the inbox channel. Two organizations: `org_a` holds an owner, an administrator, a member and a member with no membership level; `org_b` holds one administrator.
  - The real caller composition (`resolveMessagingCaller`): anonymous `401`, a held sign-in `403` with its code, and a plain member `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` naming `setup.write`, each before a membership read or a send.
  - A caller holding Setup access but not `setup.write` is refused `403`; a caller with no current organization is refused `403` before anything is read.
  - **The organization boundary of "everyone", both directions**: `org_a`'s administrator reaches exactly `org_a`'s four members (inbox rows checked: topic, title, Markdown body, severity, action URL), and nobody in `org_b`; `org_b`'s administrator reaches `org_b`'s member, the default severity `info`, and nobody in `org_a`. `emit()` is asserted to be called with `audience: 'org:members'`, `organizationId` the caller's, `actorId` the caller, `channels: ['inbox']`.
  - Picked members, one picked twice: two recipients, audience `['user:u_member', 'user:u_no_role']`.
  - A picked member of the other organization, among members of this one: refused `400` naming only that id, nothing sent, and the membership read's shape asserted (`sys_member`, `organization_id` and `$in`, `fields: ['user_id']`, `{ context: { isSystem: true } }`). `org:members`, another selector, an email address and an unknown id in `recipients` are each refused as no member.
  - Seventeen body refusals, each with its sentence and "Nothing was sent.", no `emit()`, no membership read and no inbox row: not an object; an unknown key; `organizationId` in the body; both audiences; neither; `everyone: false` with no recipients; `everyone` not a boolean; `recipients` not a list; 1,001 recipients; no title, a blank title, a title past 255; no body; an unknown severity; a `javascript:` link, a protocol-relative link, a link with a space. A query parameter refused; `503` with no messaging service; `500` when `emit()` throws.
- `in-app-message-action.test.ts` (new) pins the action against the door, so neither half can move alone: `type: 'api'`, `locations: ['list_toolbar']`, `target` equal to `IN_APP_MESSAGE_ROUTE`; `requiredPermissions` equal to `[IN_APP_MESSAGE_CAPABILITY]`, a capability whose `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` scope is `org` and which the platform administrator's grant holds; the params equal to the door's body keys, with the shapes above; the event's severity options equal to the door's severities.
- `messaging-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts`: the ledger and the registrars' enumeration agree, the new row included.

<details><summary>Ablations</summary>

Each through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on committed head `19360492` against `in-app-message-routes.ts` (anchor hit 1 → 0 on disk), running the two new test files; each restore proved by the blob hash equal to HEAD (`9d4c3105`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Control on the restored tree: 37 of 37 passed.

1. The emit's organization pinned to `org_a` (`organizationId,` → `organizationId: 'org_a',` in `inAppMessageEmitInput`): 1 failed / 36 passed, `from the other side: org_b's administrator reaches org_b's member, and nobody in org_a`.
2. The same pinned to `org_b`: 2 failed / 35 passed, `reaches every member of the sender's current organization, and nobody in the other one` and the picked-members pin.
3. The capability check off (`if (!held.includes(IN_APP_MESSAGE_CAPABILITY))` → `if (false)`): 2 failed / 35 passed, the plain member through the real composition and the Setup-access-only caller.
4. The membership check off (`outsiders = await nonMembersOf(…)` → `outsiders = []`): 5 failed / 32 passed, the other-organization member and the four non-member recipient spellings.
5. The organization filter dropped from the membership read (`{ organization_id: organizationId, user_id: { $in: chunk } }` → `{ user_id: { $in: chunk } }`): 1 failed / 36 passed, the other-organization member.
6. The door's capability moved alone (`'setup.write'` → `'setup.access'`): 4 failed / 33 passed, the action pin (`requiredPermissions` no longer the door's) and three door refusals.
7. The `user:` wrapping dropped (``message.recipients.map((id) => `user:${id}`)`` → `[...message.recipients]`): 1 failed / 36 passed, the picked-members audience pin.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **A custom permission set that grants `setup.write` is admitted too.** The gate is the capability, not a membership level: the action is listed to, and the door admits, whoever holds `setup.write` in their current organization. That is the gate the platform already declares for an organization-scoped administrative door, as ruling 6670707546 (item B) set it for the record currency backfill (`RECORD_CURRENCY_BACKFILL_CAPABILITY`), and as the organization client-address read asks it (`ORGANIZATION_CLIENT_ADDRESS_CAPABILITY`). Both organization-administrator sets and the platform administrator's grant hold it; `member_default` does not. An administrator who authors a set granting `setup.write` grants this action with it; the docs say so. A delegated administrator who holds no `setup.write` is not admitted.
- **The new REST route is public surface under `Clause-②: yes`.** `POST /api/v1/messaging/in-app-messages`, its closed body set, its refusals and its answer `{ notificationId, recipients, delivered, enqueued, failed }` are a contract from this PR on; programs and agents can call it directly, under the same rules as the action. The route ledger carries it as `server-only`.
- **"Everyone" never crosses into another organization, pinned in both directions and ablated** (ablations 1 and 2): the emit's organization is the caller's current one, never the body's, and `org:members` resolves in that organization alone (PR 1's resolver, whose own tenant-filter ablation is on #32782).
- The topic is `org.announcement`. A member whose notification preferences turn it off is not sent the message and is not counted in `recipients`.
- The door sets no cap on how many messages an administrator sends; the ruling asked for none.
- For the dialog (#32796): the form is the action's params; a plain member does not see the action; the confirmation's count is `result.recipients`; every refusal is a `400` / `403` with a sentence that says what to change.

## Verification

All readings local; every family CI runs is the PR's own check-runs.

Declared on `3bae7b7a` as `{ responses: 0, ok: 0, err: 0 }`, the preference options door's declaration (the door builds no body itself); That one-line registration in `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`, and the census entry below, are the two files outside the claimed surface. On `3bae7b7a` the derivation grows to 122 (the touched `scripts/` file brings in 18 script families): the 18 and `check:route-envelope` were run there, each `exit 0`. `--ran` over the 122: 122 derived, 122 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. Fixed on `b4d48028` by moving the census entry to that file (same count, same behaviour pin, `preference-options-routes.integration.test.ts`). The derivation on `b4d48028` is 124 families (2 new: `check-dev-prereqs --self-test`, `check:kernel-hook-pairs`, each exit 0); `--ran`: 124 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
